texts.facts: However, in terms of Section 52 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as Act, 2006), the punishment Page No.# 3/6 prescribed is now only fine upto Rs. 3 lakhs and therefore he submits that the petitioners should also get benefit of the aforesaid principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court. The learned counsel, however, has confined his argument to the sentence only. 4. To consider the aforesaid submission, this Court is to go through the complaint filed against the petitioners. The basic allegation in the complaint is to the effect that as per the Public Analyst Report dated 18.11.1988, refined vegetable oil which is sold by the petitioner is rancid and does not conform to the standard and the same is misbranded. Such materials were seized from the possession of the petitioners. Accordingly, two petitioners along with the National Co-operative Consumer's Federation of India Ltd. were prosecuted. So far relating to the accused No. 1 and 2 from whose possession, the misbranded materials were recovered i.e. petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 had preferred the present revision petition.
texts.arguments: 5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that though three of the accused person including the accused No. 3 i.e. National Co- operative Consumer's Federation of India Ltd were convicted, however, the accused No. 3, did not prefer any appeal and paid the fine. 7. Section 7 of the Act, 1954 prohibits any person to manufacture for sale or store, sell or to distribute any adulterated food and any misbranded food etc. 9. The Act, 2006 was enacted with an object to consolidate the laws relating to food and to establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for laying down science based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import, to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. Clause-(ii) of Sub Section 1 of Section 97 of the Act, 2006 on the other hand prescribes that such repeal shall not affect any right, privilege application or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under any of the enactment or orders under repeal. However, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Trilok Chand -Vs- State of Himachal Pradesh reported in 2020 10 SCC 763 referring to the earlier judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in T. Barai -Vs- Henry Ah Hoe reported in (1983) 1 SCC 177, more particularly relying on paragraph 22 of the said judgment, concluded that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused person it could be applied with respect to the earlier cases as well as which are pending in the Court. 13. Section 52 of the Act, 2006 prescribes that any person who, whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is substandard, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to five lakh rupees.
